title: Theron's Vision

narrative.text: Theron's study is buried in constitutional drafts. Every surface is covered with annotated copies of the Halvek Constitution — the original document he has spent thirty years trying to replace. He looks up when you enter, removes his glasses, and gestures to the chair across from his desk.

You have a constitutional convention to manage. I have been thinking about what the Reformists need from this document. We are your base — sixty-two seats, the intellectual foundation of this government. We need: full judicial independence through an independent commission. The bill of rights — expanded, with social and economic rights. No emergency powers — none, Chancellor. The Halvek clause must die. Civilian military oversight. And the immunity clause must be revoked. I know what Kolvar is telling you. What Kolvar wants is a document that protects his people from accountability. What Veltria needs is a document that does not flinch from the truth.

I am not demanding. I am advising. If you compromise on these points, you will still have a constitution. But you will have a constitution that looks backward — that hedges, that protects the powerful, that leaves the door open for the next Gavril Soren to walk through. That is not the Veltria I have been writing about for thirty years. But it is the Veltria you may have to govern.

monologue: Theron has been annotating the Halvek constitution for thirty years. Every margin note, every crossed-out clause, every marginalia in his precise handwriting — a monument to sustained intellectual rage. He wants the full vision: no emergency powers, no immunity, expanded rights. He calls it advising. He is not wrong about what the country needs. He may be wrong about what the votes will allow.

choices.text: "You are asking for the full Theron vision. Every progressive clause. No compromises. I want to give you that. But the votes — Theron, where are the votes? I need you to help me find them."

reactions.text: He removes his glasses and cleans them — his habitual gesture when processing something significant. I will help you find them, he says. The votes. If the vision is right, the votes will follow.

choices.text: "Theron, I agree with you. But I have eighty-eight Halvekist votes to consider. We will get judicial independence and the bill of rights. Emergency powers and immunity — I may have to compromise. Not because I agree with Kolvar. Because I need his votes to pass anything at all."

reactions.text: He puts his glasses back on. The motion is slow, deliberate. He understands the math. He does not like it. The silence is the sound of a philosopher accepting that principles sometimes require pragmatism.
